digest.headline: Alphabet and Intel lead tech stocks lower on earnings misses as the US economy grows by 3.4%.

lede.b: Alphabet and Intel saw their share prices drop because their earnings reports missed expectations, which are the official financial results companies report to the public. Wall Street, which is the main hub for American financial trading, closed lower as investors worried about spending on artificial intelligence, meaning computer systems built to mimic human thinking. Meanwhile, the U.S. economy grew at an annual rate of 3.4%, which is the measure of all goods and services produced, beating previous expectations. The S&P 500 index, a list tracking five hundred of the largest American companies, fell to 7,695.25 points. Alphabet's record sell-off, where many investors rushed to sell their shares at once, overshadowed the positive economic growth report.
lede.i: Alphabet and Intel shares declined after their earnings reports missed consensus forecasts, driving Wall Street lower amid renewed anxiety over artificial intelligence capital expenditure. The S&P 500 index fell to 7,695.25 points despite a stronger-than-expected U.S. gross domestic product expansion rate of 3.4%. Alphabet's historic sell-off completely overshadowed the positive inflation and economic growth beat during the session.
lede.a: Alphabet and Intel equities suffered severe downward pressure following earnings misses, dragging Wall Street lower as market participants repriced artificial intelligence capital expenditure risk. The S&P 500 index retreated to 7,695.25 points despite gross domestic product growth printing at an above-consensus 3.4%. Alphabet's historic equity sell-off entirely eclipsed the broader macroeconomic data release.

Intel shares fell 23.03% in after-hours trading. Wall Street ended lower as investors worried about high spending on artificial intelligence.
stories.i: Alphabet shares recorded a historic sell-off following a revenue miss. Intel shares plunged 23.03% in after-hours trading due to weak earnings figures. Wall Street closed lower as investors renewed concerns over artificial intelligence capital expenditure.
stories.a: Alphabet shares registered a record sell-off following a top-line miss. Intel shares dropped 23.03% after hours on weak guidance and bloated capex worries. Broad market indices fell as sentiment turned negative on heavy artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.

stories.t: UK Defence Contracts Introduce Strict Local Investment Rules
stories.b: The UK government announced a new Offsets policy for defence procurement. Overseas companies winning UK defence contracts must now invest their economic benefits back into the UK. This rule is designed to prioritise British jobs and skills.
stories.i: The UK government introduced a new Offsets policy for defence procurement. Overseas firms securing UK defence contracts now face mandatory requirements to invest economic benefits back into the domestic economy. These regulations aim to secure British jobs and skills.
stories.a: The UK government implemented a new Offsets policy targeting defence procurement. Foreign entities awarded UK defence contracts must repatriate economic benefits via domestic investment. The framework enforces a direct correlation between defence expenditure and the retention of domestic skills.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Bank of Japan holds rates while Tokyo inflation reaches 2.8%

stories.t: Bank of Japan Holds Interest Rates
stories.b: The Bank of Japan is the country's central bank, which is the main institution that sets monetary policy and interest rates. Officials decided to keep interest rates steady at their meeting. Traders adjusted their positions ahead of the announcement. The dollar-yen exchange rate hovered in the 157 range. Governor Ueda scheduled a press conference following the conclusion of the meeting.
stories.i: The Bank of Japan kept interest rates on hold as markets anticipated the outcome of the meeting. Traders adjusted positions ahead of the decision, leaving the dollar-yen pairing hovering in the upper 157 range. Falling U.S. Treasury yields provided support for the currency. Governor Ueda delivered remarks at a press conference following the meeting.
stories.a: The Bank of Japan maintained its policy rate while telegraphing potential future hikes, keeping the dollar-yen in the 157 range amid position squaring. Falling U.S. Treasury yields compressed rate differentials, offering marginal support to the yen. Market participants parsed Governor Ueda's press conference for clues on the timing of normalization. The implied policy path depends on wage growth matching the trajectory of inflation.

stories.t: Tokyo Inflation Rises to 2.8%
stories.b: Inflation means that prices for goods and services are going up over time. Government figures showed that consumer prices in Tokyo rose by 2.8%. The Japanese yen barely moved after the release of the new data. Traders continued to watch currency levels closely.
stories.i: Tokyo inflation accelerated to an annual rate of 2.8%. The currency market registered minimal movement in response to the release. The exchange rate remained anchored in the 157 range as traders awaited central bank commentary.
stories.a: Tokyo headline inflation printed at 2.8%, failing to catalyse a meaningful breakout in the yen. Spot FX showed negligible reaction as participants maintained existing positions ahead of the monetary policy outcome. Real yield differentials remained wide, keeping downward pressure on the currency.

politics.b: Political leaders and central bank officials met in Tokyo to manage the nation's economic policy.
politics.i: Japanese authorities monitored exchange rate movements and price stability metrics.
politics.a: Policymakers balanced currency stabilization objectives against domestic price dynamics.

timeline: Tokyo inflation data showed a rise to 2.8%.
The Bank of Japan concluded its meeting and kept interest rates on hold.

China.label: China
China.sub: Disbursements completed, earnings missed, and output slashed

stories.t: BYD Misses Earnings Estimates as EV Price War Takes Its Toll
stories.b: BYD missed estimates because an electric vehicle price war took its toll. An electric vehicle runs on a battery instead of petrol. Companies sell these cars cheaper to win buyers. This hurts their profits. BYD reported earnings that fell short of expectations.
stories.i: BYD missed earnings estimates as an intense electric vehicle price war compressed margins. Automakers are slashing prices to capture market share in a crowded sector. This aggressive discounting directly hurts profitability across the industry. BYD reported results that fell below consensus expectations.
stories.a: BYD missed consensus earnings estimates as the domestic electric vehicle price war eroded operating margins. Sustained margin compression reflects aggressive discounting strategies across the original equipment manufacturer base. This dynamic continues to impair sector-wide profitability despite high volume. BYD reported earnings that failed to meet market expectations.

stories.t: Automakers Slash China Output as Gasoline Car Market Shrinks
stories.b: Toyota, Honda, and Nissan cut their production in China. The gasoline car market is shrinking fast. People now prefer other types of cars. Car factories must make fewer vehicles to match lower demand. The Japanese companies reduced their output.
stories.i: Toyota, Honda, and Nissan slashed output in China as the gasoline car market shrank. Traditional combustion engine vehicles are losing ground to newer alternatives. Manufacturers are adjusting factory capacity to match falling demand. This contraction forced major Japanese brands to scale back local production.
stories.a: Toyota, Honda, and Nissan scaled back production in China following a structural contraction in the internal combustion engine vehicle market. Secular shifts toward alternative powertrains continue to erode legacy gasoline car sales. Manufacturers are rationalizing regional output to mitigate overcapacity risks. This capacity reduction underscores the speed at which traditional market share is evaporating.

stories.t: China Completes 800 Billion Yuan Disbursement for Projects
stories.b: China finished sending out 800 billion yuan to pay for projects. A disbursement is money paid out from a pool of funds. This cash helps build things and support the economy. The government completed the entire transfer amount. The funds are now ready to be used.
stories.i: China completed an 800 billion yuan disbursement to fund various infrastructure projects. Such a disbursement represents the physical release of capital from state treasuries to active developments. This capital injection aims to stimulate economic activity through direct investment. The government finished routing the entire allocation.
stories.a: China finalized an 800 billion yuan liquidity disbursement directed toward designated capital projects. This fiscal deployment channels state resources directly into targeted infrastructure to support macro growth. The execution of this transfer represents the full delivery of pledged development capital. Authorities completed the entire distribution cycle.

politics.b: The Chinese economy faces heavy scrutiny over unreliable data and dropping consumer demand. Observers worry that the numbers might not tell the whole truth. People are buying fewer items than before. These issues create challenges for the country.
politics.i: The Chinese economy faces intense scrutiny over unreliable economic data and dropping consumer demand. Analysts question the accuracy of official reporting metrics. Domestic consumption continues to soften across multiple retail sectors. These combined factors complicate the macroeconomic outlook.
politics.a: The Chinese macro economy faces mounting scrutiny regarding data reliability and persistent weakness in consumer demand. Market participants exhibit skepticism toward reported statistics amid structural consumption declines. Aggregate demand continues to contract across key retail segments. These headwinds complicate policy efficacy and growth forecasting.

India.label: India
India.sub: US rate pause and bond yields drive Indian share recovery

stories.t: Global Yields and US Rate Decisions Lift Domestic Equities
stories.src: The Economic Times · The Times of India
stories.b: The Sensex rose by 905 points after the United States central bank decided to pause interest rate changes. A central bank is a national institution that controls the money supply and interest rates. Lower borrowing costs in America often encourage global investors to put money back into emerging markets like India. Foreign portfolio investors slowed down their selling of Indian shares. The Sensex closed higher following these shifts.
stories.i: The Sensex advanced by 905 points following the decision by the US central bank to pause its rate tightening cycle. Lower US yields reduced the attractiveness of dollar-denominated assets and eased capital outflows. Foreign portfolio investors moderated their selling pressure, which helped lift domestic market sentiment. The broader recovery gathered pace as overseas liquidity pressures abated.
stories.a: The Sensex rallied 905 points as the US Federal Reserve enacted a rate pause and US Treasury yields dipped. Lower core yields compressed the opportunity cost of holding risk assets, triggering a tactical reversal in foreign portfolio investor liquidations. Market participants recalibrated duration risk in light of the altered Fed trajectory, allowing domestic equities to reclaim lost ground.

stories.t: Floating Rate Bond Coupon Fixed by Reserve Bank of India
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India set the interest rate for the Government of India Floating Rate Bond 2034 at 7.26% per annum. This rate applies for the half-year period running from October 30, 2026, to April 29, 2027. Floating rate bonds have interest payments that change over time based on other market benchmarks. The coupon for this specific bond relies on the average yield of recent 182-day Treasury bills. Treasury bills are short-term debt instruments issued by the government to raise money.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India fixed the coupon for the Government of India Floating Rate Bond 2034 at 7.26% per annum for the period from October 30, 2026, to April 29, 2027. This instrument adjusts its payouts according to a base rate derived from recent 182-day Treasury bill auctions. The weighted average yield of the last three Treasury bill auctions sets the benchmark for the adjustment mechanism. Such floating structures insulate fixed-income portfolios against rising yields.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India established the coupon for the Government of India Floating Rate Bond 2034 at 7.26% per annum for the semi-annual period ending April 29, 2027. The underlying pricing formula indexes the base rate to the weighted average yield of the preceding three 182-day Treasury bill auctions from the rate fixing date of October 30, 2026. This structural design transfers duration risk directly to holders while aligning semi-annual resets with short-term money market rates. The issuance mechanics reflect ongoing liquidity management through variable-rate sovereign debt.

stories.t: Market Breadth Drops Despite Headline Index Gains
stories.b: Market breadth hit a seven-month low even though major stock indices like Nifty and Sensex increased. Market breadth measures the proportion of stocks advancing versus those declining during a trading session. A low reading means that only a small group of large companies drove the index gains, while many other stocks fell or stayed flat. The Nifty recovery gathered pace toward the 23,000 mark. Investors tracked these conflicting signals ahead of the opening bell.
stories.i: Market breadth deteriorated to a seven-month low despite headline advances in the Nifty and Sensex benchmarks. Narrow participation indicates that a concentrated group of heavyweights pushed the indices higher while a majority of individual shares lagged. The Nifty recovery gathered pace toward the 23,000 threshold during the session. This divergence highlights a bifurcated equity market where index performance masks broader weakness.
stories.a: Market breadth declined to a seven-month low despite positive closes in the Nifty and Sensex. Index gains were heavily skewed toward select large-cap constituents, masking widespread selling pressure across mid- and small-cap stocks. The Nifty recovery approached the 23,000 handle amid uneven order flow distribution. Such narrow participation patterns typically signal fragile upward momentum.

politics.b: The Reserve Bank of India extended banking directions for a cooperative bank in Kerala. The central bank also set the redemption price for a sovereign gold bond tranche. Official data on external commercial borrowings for August 2026 was published.
politics.i: The Reserve Bank of India extended regulatory directions for The Irinjalakuda Town Co-operative Bank under the Banking Regulation Act. The authority also announced premature redemption pricing for the Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme 2019-20 Series VI. Separately, the central bank released foreign borrowing data for August 2026.
politics.a: The Reserve Bank of India extended statutory directions for The Irinjalakuda Town Co-operative Bank pursuant to Section 35A and Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. Concurrently, the monetary authority administered the premature redemption pricing schedule for Sovereign Gold Bond 2019-20 Series VI and published external commercial borrowing flows for August 2026.

timeline: RBI issued initial directions under Section 35A to The Irinjalakuda Town Co-operative Bank.
Government of India notified the Sovereign Gold Bond 2019-20 Series VI scheme.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras record output and oil find amid fiscal pressures

stories.t: Petrobras Hits Record Output in Third Quarter
stories.b: Petrobras is a big energy company. It reached a record production of 3.512 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in the third quarter. This output increased by 11.7% compared to the same time last year. New floating production units at fields like Búzios and Mero helped drive this growth.
stories.i: Petrobras delivered a record 3.512 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in the third quarter. This figure represents an 11.7% increase year on year. The expansion was driven by the ramp-up of new floating production storage and offloading units at the Búzios and Mero fields.
stories.a: Petrobras reported third-quarter production of 3.512 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, marking an 11.7% year-on-year expansion. Volume growth was supported by the sequential integration of new floating production storage and offloading units across the Búzios and Mero fields. Operating performance faced headwinds from softer global crude benchmarks and domestic political overhang.

stories.t: New Oil Discovery Off Amapá State
stories.b: Petrobras found a third oil-bearing interval off the coast of Amapá state. The discovery was made in a specific block in that region. Vast Conducts also completed three simultaneous oil transfers at the Port of Açu.
stories.i: Petrobras confirmed a third oil-bearing interval in an offshore block near Amapá state. Concurrently, Vast executed three simultaneous oil transfers at the Port of Açu for the first time. These operational milestones coincide with wider market pressures on local assets.
stories.a: Petrobras extended its exploration footprint by identifying a third oil-bearing interval within an offshore block in the Amapá state basin. Meanwhile, Vast operationalized three simultaneous crude transfers at the Port of Açu. These developments unfold against a backdrop of a softer oil tape and ongoing fiscal concerns.

politics.b: The Brazilian real weakened because people worry about government spending and public debts. The Ibovespa stock market index dropped to a three-month low.
politics.i: Persistent fiscal concerns caused the Brazilian real to weaken against major currencies. The Ibovespa index dropped to a three-month low as investors reacted to these budgetary pressures.
politics.a: Ongoing fiscal concerns weighed on local sentiment, driving the Brazilian real lower. The Ibovespa index touched a three-month low as domestic risk premia expanded.

timeline: Petrobras reports third-quarter production of 3.512 million barrels of oil equivalent per day.
Petrobras announces a third oil discovery in a block off Amapá state.
The Ibovespa index hits a three-month low amid fiscal concerns and a weakening real.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Aramco facilities targeted in recent attacks

stories.t: Houthi Attacks Target Saudi Oil Infrastructure
stories.b: Houthis claim several attacks on Saudi oil refineries and airports in Riyadh and Dammam. Sites in Abqaiq and Shaybah are also targeted by strikes. Two people die after a drone is intercepted near the Shaybah oilfield. Saudi Aramco's headquarters suffers extensive damage.
stories.i: The Houthis claim strikes on six sites in Saudi Arabia, including international airports and Saudi Aramco facilities. The Abqaiq facility and the Shaybah oilfield experience reported drone activity, resulting in two fatalities near Shaybah. Saudi Aramco's headquarters sustains extensive damage during these incidents.
stories.a: A coordinated series of Houthi strikes target multiple Saudi energy and military installations, encompassing the Abqaiq plant and the Shaybah oilfield. Interception activity near Shaybah results in two deaths, while Saudi Aramco's headquarters suffers extensive structural damage. These multi-site claims extend to international airports in Riyadh and Dammam.

stories.t: Saudi Aramco Adjusts Cargo Sales and Supplies
stories.b: Saudi Aramco offers spot oil cargoes to European buyers. The company CEO states that replenishing crude and fuel supplies could take two years. Spot oil cargoes are individual shipments of oil sold outside long-term contracts.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco offers spot oil cargoes directly to European buyers. The chief executive officer states that replenishing crude and fuel supplies could require a two-year timeframe. These spot market offerings run alongside ongoing supply management assessments.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco initiates spot oil cargo offerings directed at European buyers. Management indicates that rebuilding depleted crude and fuel inventories will extend over a two-year horizon. This operational timeline underscores the scale of required supply replenishment.

politics.b: Attacks hit several locations in Saudi Arabia. Officials deal with security and supply challenges.
politics.i: Houthi strikes target multiple energy and transport sites across the kingdom. Saudi Aramco manages infrastructure damage and supply replenishment timelines.
politics.a: Multi-site Houthi strikes impact key petroleum infrastructure and transport hubs. Saudi Aramco navigates structural repairs at its headquarters alongside extended inventory replenishment horizons.

timeline: Houthis claim strikes on multiple Saudi energy and military sites.
Two people are killed near the Shaybah oilfield after a drone interception.
Saudi Aramco offers spot oil cargoes to European buyers.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira gains against the dollar amid low turnover

stories.t: Naira Rises Against Dollar
stories.src: Daily Post Nigeria · MarketForces Africa · PM News Nigeria
stories.b: The naira is the official money used in Nigeria. It grew stronger against the United States dollar for the fourth day in a row on October 29, 2026. The exchange rate improved by 5.34 naira per dollar. At the same time, the total amount of money traded in the interbank market dropped by 80%.
stories.i: The naira recorded its fourth consecutive appreciation against the US dollar on October 29, 2026. The currency gained 5.34 naira during the session. This upward movement coincided with an 80% decline in interbank foreign exchange turnover.
stories.a: The naira advanced against the US dollar for the fourth consecutive session on October 29, 2026, with an incremental gain of 5.34 naira. This price action occurred alongside an 80% contraction in interbank foreign exchange turnover, illustrating liquidity constraints in the spot market.

stories.t: Skyway Aviation Reports Earnings
stories.b: Skyway Aviation shared its financial results for the first nine months of 2026. The company brought in 11.23 billion naira in revenue. It also posted an operating profit before tax of 2.33 billion naira.
stories.i: Skyway Aviation published its financial figures for January to September 2026. The company generated 11.23 billion naira in revenue. Operating profit before tax reached 2.33 billion naira for the period.
stories.a: Skyway Aviation reported revenue of 11.23 billion naira for the January-September 2026 period. Operating profit before tax printed at 2.33 billion naira over the same timeframe.

politics.b: Governor Otti gave 10 million naira to help rebuild Ngwa High School. A school alumni group also planned a 1.5 billion naira development fund for their 50th anniversary. Meanwhile, an official stated that a shipping fund is kept in naira instead of dollars.
politics.i: Governor Otti pledged 10 million naira to rehabilitate Ngwa High School. The Progressive Old Students' Association announced a 1.5 billion naira development fund for its 50th anniversary. A former NIMASA chief clarified that the cabotage vessel fund is held in naira rather than dollars.
politics.a: Governor Otti committed 10 million naira toward the rehabilitation of Ngwa High School. Concurrently, the Progressive Old Students' Association scheduled a 1.5 billion naira development fund launch for its 50th anniversary. A former NIMASA executive noted that the cabotage vessel fund remains denominated in naira rather than US dollars.

timeline: Governor Otti pledged 10 million naira to rehabilitate Ngwa High School.
